step_by_step_reasoning: A scheduled CloudWatch Event kicks off an AWS Step Functions state machine. This workflow coordinates three Lambda functions: first, querying the 3rd-party drone image API; second, copying new imagery from the 3rd-party platform into an S3 bucket; and third, generating raster proxy files registered in the on-premises database. The on-premises server accesses the physical image files in S3 through AWS Storage Gateway. Finally, internal operations users query the on-premises mapping server to view the well pad images.

graph.name: Marathon Oil Serverless Drone Imagery Ingestion and Mapping Pipeline
graph.notes: Automates ingestion of drone-captured well pad imagery from a third-party platform into AWS S3, utilizing Lambda to create raster proxies for on-premises GIS systems accessing files via Storage Gateway.

nodes.name: CloudWatch Event
nodes.notes: Triggers the Step Functions workflow on a scheduled basis.

nodes.name: Image Ingestion Orchestrator
nodes.notes: Orchestrates the sequence of Lambda functions to process new flight images.

nodes.name: Processing Lambdas
nodes.notes: Three Lambda functions to poll API, transfer images to S3, and write raster proxies to the local server database.

nodes.name: Drone Image Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores high-resolution ortho mosaics, digital terrain models, and digital elevation models.

nodes.name: File Gateway
nodes.notes: Enables the on-premises mapping software to mount and read files directly from the S3 bucket.

nodes.name: 3rd Party Drone Software
nodes.notes: Processes raw drone imagery and stores processed flights.

nodes.name: On-Prem Mapping Server & DB
nodes.notes: Hosts the legacy GIS/mapping software and database storing image raster proxies.

nodes.name: Operations & Maintenance Teams
nodes.notes: Internal users accessing the GIS platform to perform equipment health checks and preventive maintenance.

edges.notes: Triggers orchestration workflow on a schedule.
